research_direction: RGB occluded person ReID; identity-by-donor-patch content interaction study
hypothesis: Under fixed occlusion geometry, changing cross-image donor-patch content may perturb identity features differently for different target identities. Penalizing the 2x2 difference-in-differences may reduce identity-conditioned interference while allowing a shared additive donor-patch effect.
status_and_novelty_boundary: A testable project-specific hypothesis, not an established novel contribution. Factorial invariance, interaction suppression, counterfactual ReID and donor-patch augmentation have broader prior art; no priority or novelty claim is permitted without a dedicated search and independent confirmation.
development_occlusion_mode: Deterministic rectangular donor-patch queries. Donor images come only from Market training identities, disjoint from held-out development identities. The same filename, area, donor list, location and donor index mapping is shared by every model.
initialization: Official OSNet x1.0 ImageNet pretrained weights; same identity split, initialization source and paired random seed per comparison.
identity_split: Reuse deterministic Market-1501 training identity split from training_split(seed=2026): 651 train IDs and 100 held-out development IDs. Development queries use all images from one deterministic camera per identity; gallery uses other cameras.
optimizer: Adam AMSGrad, backbone lr 0.0003, FC/classifier lr 0.0015, weight decay 0.0005, cosine schedule, first two epochs freeze OSNet feature extractor, AMP, gradient clip 10.
loss: Label-smoothed identity CE (0.1) + 0.5 batch-hard triplet (margin 0.3). Pairwise consistency adds 0.5 times mean same-image cross-donor cosine distance. Factorial interaction adds 0.5 times squared L2 norm of (z_A,d1-z_A,d2)-(z_B,d1-z_B,d2), using L2-normalized embeddings.
factorial_intervention: For each group, two target identities and two donor identities share one fixed rectangle. The same image crop from each donor is pasted into the same rectangle on both target identities, yielding A/d1, A/d2, B/d1, B/d2. Donor crops are not segmented into pure occluder pixels and may contain person or background content. Each of the six sampled identities participates in four target pairs per optimizer step. Identity and donor main effects are permitted; only their interaction is penalized.
primary_development_metric: Mean mAP of fixed 30% and 50% rectangular donor-patch query occlusion, averaged across five paired seeds. Clean mAP, Rank-1/5, mINP and per-seed differences are secondary.
external_plan: After all twenty development runs complete, freeze protocol/source, every image-content SHA256 and checkpoint SHA256, then evaluate every checkpoint on all 1000 Occluded-REID occluded queries against all 1000 whole gallery images. No target training, reranking, flip, model selection or hyperparameter changes.
external_prior_exposure: Occluded-REID results were inspected in earlier stages; this is exploratory transfer evidence only, never a blind confirmation set.
decision_rule: Retain all registered arms and seeds. Report matched paired deltas, mean and sample standard deviation, all per-seed results, actual optimizer updates and update skips. Five seeds are screening evidence, not a significance test or SOTA claim.
comparison_scope: The OSNet x1.0 backbone, split, optimizer, update count, source sampler, image transforms and augmentation budget are fixed. Plain is the clean-input reference; the three occlusion arms process 48 views per optimizer update.
related_work_boundary: This is not CLCP/reliability pooling, high-frequency token selection, prompt learning, feature completion or Mamba. COPE (CVPR 2026) uses cross-identity shared occlusion consistency; FLaN-Net (IJCAI 2025) uses categorical prompts and uncertainty-weighted features; AHT (ECCV 2024) selects high-frequency tokens; counterfactual ReID and donor-patch augmentation also have prior art. The present test studies a paired identity-by-donor-patch interaction term, but its novelty remains unresolved.
implementation_note: SemanticDetailFusion, the single-layer Transformer, and v4 MDTA are excluded as method arms because available evidence is unstable and their mechanism novelty is not established.
